title: Affine zero-section orientation comparison and global descent
statement:
Fix the finite purity datum [def-pur-conventions]: $p$ prime, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth separated finite-type morphisms of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and $\omega_h=Rh^!\Lambda$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Let $\vartheta_h:\omega_h\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(m_h)[2m_h]$ be the specified diagonal orientations [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object], with $m_f=d,m_g=e,m_{gf}=d+e$. Let $\sigma=c_{g,f,\Lambda}^{-1}\theta_{f,\omega_g}\mathrm{sym}$ be the tensor comparison [lem-pur-composition-tensor-mate], and use the compatible affine charts and the maps $\alpha_h,\delta_h,\beta_h,\kappa,\nu_{d,e}$ specified in [lem-pur-composition-compatible-dnc-charts].

Let
$$\mu:\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\otimes^LLf^*\Lambda_Y(e)[2e]\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X(d+e)[2d+2e]$$
be concatenation of the nonnegative tensor powers defining the twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with the canonical twist pullback [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists], derived tensor/shift reassociation, and addition of shifts. This yields, naturally for every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the canonical source isomorphism
$$I_K:L(gf)^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*(Lg^*K(e)[2e])(d)[2d],$$
using the pullback compositor [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Its ordered factors are the canonical source comparison of [def-pur-composition-comparisons]. The sign for interchanging the blocks shifted by $2d,2e$ is $(-1)^{(2d)(2e)}=+1$.

For any affine finite-type $k$-scheme $B$, write $P_r:\mathbf A^r_B\to B$, $z_r:B\to\mathbf A^r_B$, $D_r=Lz_r^*\omega_{P_r}$ [def-sbc-affine-space, def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section], and let $\Gamma_{P_r,\Lambda}$ be the ordered affine comparison [def-pur-affine-space-comparison], extended to every $n\geq1$ as in [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement]. Put $b_r=Lz_r^*(\Gamma_{P_r,\Lambda}^{-1})$ with twist restriction. For $q:\mathbf A^{d+e}_B\to\mathbf A^e_B$, the specified comparisons satisfy
$$\Gamma_{P_{d+e},\Lambda}^{-1}\sigma_{q,P_e}=\mu(\Gamma_{q,\Lambda}^{-1}\otimes Lq^*\Gamma_{P_e,\Lambda}^{-1}),\qquad b_{d+e}\nu_{d,e}=\mu(b_d\otimes b_e).$$
Here the orientation of $q$ is the base change of the rank-$d$ bundle orientation; the same formulas hold for $d=0$ or $e=0$ with $\Gamma_{P_0,-}=1$ and the unit laws. These identities involve the integration-normalized orientations, not independently chosen bundle trivializations.

On each compatible chart of $X$, the normal-bundle orientations are these $b_r$, and
$$\beta_{gf}\delta_{gf}\kappa=\mu((\beta_f\delta_f)\otimes Lf^*(\beta_g\delta_g)).$$
Globally one has
$$(**)\qquad\vartheta_{gf}\sigma=\mu(\vartheta_f\otimes Lf^*\vartheta_g).$$
The local-to-global assertion here includes the following detection property. Put $T_X=\Lambda_X(d+e)[2d+2e]$. Its common-shift removal is a locally free rank-one coefficient sheaf in degree zero. Restriction of $\operatorname{Aut}_{D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)}(T_X)$ to the covering charts above is injective. In particular the automorphism $(\vartheta_{gf}\sigma)[\mu(\vartheta_f\otimes Lf^*\vartheta_g)]^{-1}$ is the identity. The displayed global identity also holds for empty $X$.

proof.text: Apply the affine integration orientation lemma to obtain the same normalized Gamma family for both ranks, its affine and zero-section equations, and all beta frame identifications.
The chosen unique source comparison satisfies its normalization by choose_spec. Apply eight-factor naturality to all finite-Tor inputs. The even-block sign is one because (-1)^2=1.
Apply the chart assembly lemma to the zero-section equation and the beta identifications on all affine pairs. Keep the beta identifications themselves as the second local conclusion.

Apply the Tate detection lemma and then chart descent to get the global orientation equality. Substitute it in the quotient equation and cancel the inverse tensor orientation and inverse mu by the isomorphism identities. Assemble all conjuncts with the same normalized Gamma family.
